transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’ve just been feeling really down on myself. Like, I know things go wrong for everyone, but I keep feeling like it’s all somehow my fault. At work I feel like I’m a bad employee, and with my house… like I’m failing at that too, like I deserve to lose what I worked for. I know that probably sounds dramatic, sorry. I just haven’t been able to shake it.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

I think it kind of started after I bought my townhouse. Not right that second, but once the pressure of keeping up with everything started building, it just… settled in. It’s been going on for about two years and a few months now—maybe two years and three months. I hope that makes sense.
During the past two years, have you felt down or depressed most days?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the depression and not really enjoying things like I used to has been there most days for about two years and one month. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During the last two years, was there ever a time when you felt free of these depressive feelings for more than two months?

Not really, no. I mean, there were little stretches where I could function a bit better and maybe not feel it as strongly, but I don’t think I ever had more than two months where it was actually gone. Looking back, it’s kind of been there most of the time.
During this time, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your depression felt clearly worse than usual?

Yeah… I think there were times when it felt heavier than my usual, but honestly the depression and not really being interested in things has kind of been there pretty consistently for about two years and one month. I’m not sure if I’m answering exactly what you’re asking, but it hasn’t really felt like it fully let up.
During this time, have you generally had low self-esteem?

Yeah… I guess I have. I try not to think of it as “low self-esteem,” exactly, but I do feel like when things go wrong it must be because I messed up. Like I’m not doing well enough at work, or I’m failing at taking care of my home… and then it turns into this feeling that maybe I deserve to lose the things I worked for. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but that’s where my mind goes.
During this time, have you often felt hopeless?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t always call it hopeless, because I can still, like, get through the day and do what I’m supposed to do. But I came in because I can’t seem to stop thinking that when something goes wrong, it’s my fault… like I’m just a bad employee, or I’m not handling being a homeowner the way I should.

And then it kind of turns into this feeling that maybe I deserve to lose the things I worked for. I know that sounds harsh, sorry… but that’s the thought I keep getting stuck on.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

I don’t know if I’d say “a lot of different things,” exactly. I mean, I do worry, but it’s usually about whether I’m doing things right or messing something up. I’m not sure if that counts as excessive… sorry, I’m trying to answer it the way you mean.
Do these feelings mainly come up when you think about your townhouse and the responsibilities that came with it?

Kind of, yes… the townhouse is a big part of it, because it feels like proof that I’m either handling my life or I’m not. But it’s not only that. It spills over into work too, like if anything goes wrong I immediately think it’s because I failed somehow… like I’m a bad employee, or I shouldn’t have taken on being a homeowner.

I know that’s probably not the most balanced way to see it, but I keep getting stuck on this thought that I deserve to lose what I worked for. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
If the stress around the townhouse were taken away, do you think these feelings would mostly go away?

I wish I could say yes, because that would make it simpler. The townhouse definitely makes it louder, if that makes sense. But I don’t think it would mostly go away.

Even when it’s work stuff, or just anything that doesn’t go right, I go straight to thinking it’s my fault… like I’m not doing enough, or I’m bad at the things I’m supposed to be responsible for. And then I get this really ugly thought that maybe I deserve to lose what I worked for.

I know that sounds dramatic. I’m sorry. But no, I don’t think taking away just the townhouse stress would fix it completely.
During this period, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when your depression was clearly worse than your usual baseline?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it’s hard for me to separate out what’s “baseline” anymore, because the depression and not really enjoying things have kind of been there for a long time now—about two years and a month, I’d say.

So… yes, there have been stretches where it felt clearly worse, but honestly the low mood itself has been pretty constant for that whole time. Does that answer what you’re asking?
During one of those times when your depression felt clearly worse than usual, did you have thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t think I want to hurt myself, if that’s what you mean. I haven’t really thought of it as a plan or anything like that.

There have been moments where I’ve felt really tired of myself, or like people might be better off not having to deal with me, but I don’t know if that counts as “better off dead.” I’m sorry, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
During one of those times when your depression felt clearly worse than usual, did it last at least two weeks?

Yes… it did. I mean, I think it’s been more than just a two-week thing, honestly. The depression and not really having interest in things has been there for about two years and a month.

There are worse stretches inside that, but the overall feeling has lasted a lot longer than two weeks. Does that make sense?
During one of those clearly worse periods, did your sleep change noticeably?

Yes… yeah, I think it did. I mean, I still got some sleep, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most nights I’d be lying there for hours just listening to the house settle.

And then I’d wake up around three or four in the morning and just… not really be able to get back to sleep before work. Is that the kind of sleep change you mean?
During one of those worse periods, did your appetite change noticeably?

Yeah… I guess it did. I don’t always notice it right away, because it feels like I’m just busy or not thinking about food, but during those worse times I’ll skip actual meals during the day.

It’s kind of embarrassing, but I’ll end up mostly having coffee, maybe toast, and then whatever is easiest later. And then I’ll notice my clothes feel looser and realize I haven’t really been eating normally. Is that the kind of change you mean?
During one of those worse periods, did you feel slowed down in your body or movements, or so restless that you couldn’t sit still?

Um… more slowed down, I think. Not really restless.

I try not to make a big thing of it, because I still get myself to work, but some mornings everything feels like it takes so much effort. Like opening spreadsheets, typing out replies, even walking to a meeting… it feels like I’m pushing through wet cement.

I don’t know if other people notice it, or if I just feel it internally, but it’s definitely there during the worse periods.
During one of those worse periods, did you have trouble concentrating?

I… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I have days where I’m not as sharp, but I don’t know if it’s enough to call it “trouble concentrating.”

At work I can usually still get through things if I make lists or reread emails a couple times. It’s more like I feel foggy, maybe, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Does that count as what you’re asking about?
During one of those worse periods, did you feel unusually tired or low on energy?

I don’t know… I mean, I feel tired sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s unusual exactly. It’s hard to separate from just work and not sleeping perfectly, you know?

During those worse periods I probably do feel more drained, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic. I can still do what I need to do, mostly. So… maybe some low energy, but I’m not sure if it’s the kind you mean.
During one of those worse periods, did you feel depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t love saying it that way, because I’ve been trying to keep functioning and not make it sound worse than it is, but the depressed feeling and not really being interested in things has been there for… about two years and a month now.

It’s not like every single minute is equally bad, but during the worse stretches, yes, it’s most of the day, nearly every day. Does that make sense?
During one of those worse periods, did you feel worthless?

Yeah… I guess I do. I don’t really like saying “worthless,” because that sounds… extreme, and I know I’m supposed to be more reasonable about it.

But during those worse times, I keep feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like I’m failing at work, or I’m a bad employee, and even with my house I feel like I’m this bad homeowner who doesn’t deserve to keep what I’ve worked for. I know that probably sounds harsh, but that’s where my mind goes.

During those worse periods I probably do feel more drained, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic. I can still do what I need to do, mostly. So… maybe some low energy, but I’m not sure if it’s the kind you mean.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient had depressed mood nearly every day during the same at-least-2-week worse period, to confirm a major depressive episode superimposed on persistent depressive disorder versus persistent depressive disorder alone.
doctor.question: During one of those worse periods, did you feel depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression and loss of interest have been with me for about two years and one month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the presence and persistence of depressed mood during worse periods, which is covered by the depressive episode duration profile indicating depression has been present for about two years and one month.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I don’t love saying it that way, because I’ve been trying to keep functioning and not make it sound worse than it is, but the depressed feeling and not really being interested in things has been there for… about two years and a month now.

It’s not like every single minute is equally bad, but during the worse stretches, yes, it’s most of the day, nearly every day. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient had a full major depressive episode during the chronic depressive period, which best distinguishes persistent depressive disorder from recurrent major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: During one of those worse periods, did you feel worthless?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault, like I’m a bad employee and a bad homeowner who deserves to lose what I worked for.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether the patient felt worthless during worse periods, which matches the Worthlessness_Guilt symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess I do. I don’t really like saying “worthless,” because that sounds… extreme, and I know I’m supposed to be more reasonable about it.

But during those worse times, I keep feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like I’m failing at work, or I’m a bad employee, and even with my house I feel like I’m this bad homeowner who doesn’t deserve to keep what I’ve worked for. I know that probably sounds harsh, but that’s where my mind goes.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronic depressed mood with anhedonia present most days for over 2 years, without any remission longer than 2 months, along with persistent low self-esteem and hopelessness, which supports persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). There are also superimposed periods of worsening lasting at least 2 weeks with additional depressive symptoms (sleep disturbance, reduced appetite/weight loss, psychomotor slowing, worthlessness), but the overall course is chronically persistent rather than clearly episodic, making F34.1 the best fit over recurrent major depressive disorder.
